activities.anchor: myth is not a false story
activities.caption: file each narrative by its function
activities.name: mrsMythSort

config.prompt: Comparative mythology classifies by function — file each:

items.label: how the world began — from nothing, from chaos, from a cosmic egg
creation from the body of a slain primordial being
'we do this because...' — explaining why a practice exists
why the ritual must be performed this way

config.why: The Genesis narratives, the Qurʾanic retellings, the Exodus, the Ramayana and the Dreaming songs all do this work: they tell a community what kind of world it lives in.

activities.anchor: calling Genesis, the Exodus or the Ramayana a myth means
activities.caption: fill the blanks — what the technical term does
activities.name: mrsRegisterCloze

config.text: The technical term classifies a story's %%0%%; it does not adjudicate its %%1%% accuracy.
config.hint: What the classification sorts by — and the register of truth it refuses to judge.

activities.caption: pair each architectural feature with what it encodes
activities.name: mrsSpaceMatch

config.prompt: A building is a cosmological diagram — pair each feature with its encoding:

pairs.right: toward the rising sun and the resurrection
a screen of icons making the transition between worlds visible
holds the Torah scrolls at the front facing Jerusalem

config.why: Three traditions, one grammar: the building tells you, without a word, what is most real and where you stand relative to it.

activities.anchor: Artefacts and ritual dress are the same diagram in miniature
activities.caption: drag the divider — the same objects, two readings
activities.name: mrsVisitorCompare

config.prompt: One object, two readers — drag the divider.

before.label: The trained worshipper
before.text: The crucifix condenses the Passion narrative; the tasbih beads pace the remembrance of God; the tallit and tefillin make doctrine literally wearable — the body itself a ritual instrument.

after.label: The untrained visitor
after.text: The same objects read as mere decoration — the meaning lives in the trained community, not the object.

config.why: A symbol system is learned, which is why the same object consoles one worshipper and means nothing to another.

activities.caption: true or false — what ritual does
activities.name: mrsRitualJudge

statements.s: Ritual does not merely represent — it does.
statements.why: Marriage, initiation, mourning: rites accomplish transitions that ordinary time cannot.

statements.s: Communal worship creates and maintains the community through shared, ordered time.
statements.why: Durkheim's insight: in such rites the group effectively worships itself, the symbols standing for society.

statements.s: Turner's frame fits only small-scale village ritual.
statements.why: Pilgrimages, festivals, military basic training, even raves — the structure travels.

statements.s: Private worship internalises the same structures as communal worship.
statements.why: Morning prayer, voluntary night prayers, blessings over food, the home's Friday night table.

activities.caption: file each practice under its authority model
activities.name: mrsLeaderSort

config.prompt: Three models of who may stand between the ordinary and the sacred — file each:

items.label: ordination as a permanent change in the person, who alone may consecrate the Eucharist
bishops, priests and deacons forming a hierarchy of sacramental authority
any competent Muslim may lead prayer; the imam's authority is knowledge and appointment
learned authority (ulama) resting on scholarly chains of transmission
semikhah — ordination through a lineage of scholars
the leader facilitates rather than mediates; any ten adults (a minyan) suffice

config.why: Priest, imam, rabbi: sacrament, knowledge, interpretation — each model encodes a theology of mediation.

activities.caption: find the faulty line — a theorists briefing
activities.name: mrsTheorySpot

config.prompt: One line of this briefing on the grand theorists is wrong — click it:
lines: Campbell's monomyth proposed one deep pattern — departure, initiation, return — and Lucas credited it for Star Wars.
The folklorist critique: Campbell cherry-picked variants that fit and flattened culturally specific meanings into a modern psychological universal.
Eliade's sacred/profane framework proved immensely fertile for describing space, time and symbol.
Jonathan Z. Smith's rebuke was that the map IS the territory — Eliade's generalisations were sound.
config.correction: Smith's rebuke was the opposite — 'the map is not the territory': Eliade over-generalised from favoured examples and smuggled religious commitments into ostensibly neutral comparison.
config.why: The mature position: neither credulous pattern-hunting nor dismissal — each analysis must be earned case by case.

activities.anchor: Eliade's claim that ritual returns the community to mythic time
activities.caption: rebuild the Christian year in sequence
activities.name: mrsCalendarOrder

config.prompt: A walk through the foundational narrative — order the Christian year:
items: Holy Week and Easter — death and resurrection, the myth's centre
Pentecost — the Spirit founding the church
config.why: Sacred calendars are myth made into shared time: the community does not merely remember its story — it is placed inside it annually. Each Sunday Eucharist, in most theologies, is a 'little Easter' re-entering that centre.
